decisions.label: AC-2
decisions.title: Account Management
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: The image has no account of its own to manage: it ships no authentication configuration, no account store, and no management interface, and answers every request anonymously. The identity it runs as is the platform's: a numeric, non-root UID in group 0 (IMG-11), and any arbitrary UID the platform assigns (IMG-12). Account management for that identity is the platform's and the organization's, which the control baseline records as organization-inherited elsewhere.
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: AC-2(1)
decisions.title: Automated System Account Management
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: There is no account store to manage by automated means; see AC-2. The image adds none.
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: AC-2(2)
decisions.title: Automated Temporary and Emergency Account Management
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: There are no temporary or emergency accounts: the image issues no credentials of any kind; see AC-2.
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: AC-2(3)
decisions.title: Disable Accounts
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: There is no account to disable; see AC-2. The runtime identity is created and removed with the container, by the platform.
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: AC-2(4)
decisions.title: Automated Audit Actions
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: No account is created, modified, or removed in the image, so there is no such action to log; see AC-2. What the image does log is every request (AU-2).
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: AC-2(5)
decisions.title: Inactivity Logout
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: The image holds no logon session to end on inactivity; HTTP requests are stateless and anonymous; see AC-2.
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: AC-2(11)
decisions.title: Usage Conditions
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: The image enforces no per-account usage conditions because it has no accounts; see AC-2. What may be requested, and from where, is the deployment's network policy (PLT-10).
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: AC-2(12)
decisions.title: Account Monitoring for Atypical Usage
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: There is no account whose usage could be atypical; see AC-2. Request-level monitoring is the platform's (PLT-16).
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: AC-3
decisions.title: Access Enforcement
decisions.rationale: Which content is served, and to whom, is the deployment's mounted content and configuration.
decisions.statement: The image enforces what nginx enforces: it serves only files under the document root it ships, resolving each request with try_files and answering 404 otherwise, and it reads nothing outside that root. Which content exists, and who may reach it, is decided by what the deployment mounts and by its network policy (PLT-10); the image adds no access-control rules of its own.
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: AC-6(1)
decisions.title: Authorize Access to Security Functions
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: The image separates no security functions by account because it has no accounts; see AC-2. It runs with every Linux capability dropped and no_new_privileges set, verified at runtime (IMG-13), so no process holds privilege to authorize.
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: AC-6(2)
decisions.title: Non-privileged Access for Nonsecurity Functions
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: Every process in the image runs as the same unprivileged, non-root identity; there is no privileged account to use for anything, security-related or not (IMG-11, IMG-13).
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: AC-6(3)
decisions.title: Network Access to Privileged Commands
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: The image exposes no privileged command, locally or over the network: it has no shell service, no administration endpoint, and no remote-administration daemon (IMG-27).
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: AC-6(5)
decisions.title: Privileged Accounts
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: There is no privileged account to restrict: the image runs non-root with no capabilities, and carries neither su nor sudo, which the smoke suite verifies (IMG-09, IMG-11, IMG-13).
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: AC-6(9)
decisions.title: Log Use of Privileged Functions
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: No privileged function executes in the image, so there is none to log; see AC-6(5). Every request it does serve is logged (AU-2, AU-12).
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: AC-7
decisions.title: Unsuccessful Logon Attempts
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: There is no logon to attempt, successfully or otherwise; the image authenticates nobody; see AC-2.
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: AC-8
decisions.title: System Use Notification
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: The image displays no system-use notification because it has no logon and no interactive session; see AC-2. Any banner in served content is the deployment's content.
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: AC-10
decisions.title: Concurrent Session Control
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: The image controls no concurrent sessions by account, having none; see AC-2. Concurrent connections are bounded by worker_connections in the shipped configuration and by the deployment's resource limits (PLT-05).
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: AC-12
decisions.title: Session Termination
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: There is no user session to terminate; each HTTP request is answered and closed, and idle connections end at nginx's keepalive timeout (SC-10); see AC-2.
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: AC-14
decisions.title: Permitted Actions Without Identification or Authentication
decisions.rationale: The image serves its content without identification by design; the deployment decides what content that is.
decisions.statement: The image serves its content without identification or authentication by design, which is what this control requires be documented and deliberate: it is a public, read-only HTTP server. Which content may be reached without authentication is the deployment's, through what it mounts and its network policy (PLT-10).
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: AC-17(2)
decisions.title: Protection of Confidentiality and Integrity Using Encryption
decisions.rationale: TLS is enabled by mounting a server block, certificate, and key (IMG-16); the deployment chooses to.
decisions.statement: The image can protect remote access with TLS 1.2 or 1.3 when the deployment mounts a server block, certificate, and key read-only into /etc/nginx (IMG-16, IMG-17); the smoke suite proves it serves HTTPS that way. Whether remote access is encrypted in a given deployment is that deployment's decision, with the platform's (PLT-10).
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: AU-2
decisions.title: Event Logging
decisions.rationale: nginx logs every request to standard output and every error to standard error.
decisions.statement: nginx logs every request to standard output in its combined format, and every error to standard error at notice level, as the shipped nginx.conf sets. The image writes no log file, and the smoke suite reads a served request back out of the container's standard output (IMG-19).

decisions.label: AU-3
decisions.title: Content of Audit Records
decisions.rationale: Each access record states the client, time, request, status, size, referrer, and user agent.
decisions.statement: Each access record carries the client address, the time, the request line, the status, the bytes sent, the referrer, and the user agent, which is nginx's combined format, the shipped default. Error records carry the time, severity, message, client, and request (IMG-19).

decisions.label: AU-3(1)
decisions.title: Additional Audit Information
decisions.rationale: The deployment may extend nginx's log format with further fields.
decisions.statement: The image logs the combined format and adds nothing further. A deployment that needs more fields, such as a request identifier or upstream timing, mounts a server block setting its own log_format (IMG-16); the image neither prevents nor performs that.

decisions.label: AU-10
decisions.title: Non-repudiation
decisions.rationale: The image serves anonymous requests; there is no individual whose actions must be undeniable.
decisions.statement: The image serves anonymous requests and binds no action to an individual, so there is no actor whose denial the image could refute. Non-repudiation of what the image itself produces is met at release instead: every published image is signed keylessly and carries attested provenance (IMG-22).

decisions.label: AU-12
decisions.title: Audit Record Generation
decisions.rationale: Audit records are generated for every request, with nothing to enable.
decisions.statement: Audit records are generated for every request and every error as the image runs, with nothing to enable and no way to disable it short of changing the configuration: logging is compiled into the shipped nginx.conf, and the smoke suite verifies records appear on the standard streams (IMG-19).

decisions.label: CM-6
decisions.title: Configuration Settings
decisions.rationale: The image ships a reviewed configuration, but no SCAP rule selection yet evidences its settings (IMG-T3).
decisions.statement: The image ships one reviewed configuration file, owned by root and not writable by the runtime identity (IMG-10), with settings chosen for this standard: logs to the standard streams, server_tokens off, every writable path under the declared tmpfs, and listeners above 1024. What is not yet true is automated verification of those settings against a published benchmark; that waits on the SCAP profile (IMG-T3), which is why this control stays open.

decisions.label: CM-6(1)
decisions.title: Automated Management, Application, and Verification
decisions.rationale: As CM-6: automated verification of settings awaits the SCAP profile (IMG-T3).
decisions.statement: As CM-6: the settings are fixed in the image and verified by the smoke suite in the properties they produce, but not yet by an automated check against a benchmark. The SCAP profile (IMG-T3) is the work that would close it.

decisions.label: IA-2
decisions.title: Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users)
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: The image identifies and authenticates no user: it has no logon, no session, and no credential store, and serves every request anonymously; see AC-2. Identifying the people who administer the platform is the platform's and the organization's.
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: IA-2(1)
decisions.title: Multi-factor Authentication to Privileged Accounts
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: There is no privileged account, and so no multi-factor authentication for one; see IA-2 and AC-6(5).
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: IA-2(2)
decisions.title: Multi-factor Authentication to Non-privileged Accounts
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: There is no non-privileged account to authenticate, with one factor or several: the image serves every request anonymously and holds no credential store; see IA-2.
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: IA-2(5)
decisions.title: Individual Authentication with Group Authentication
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: The image uses no group authenticator, having no authentication at all; see IA-2.
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: IA-2(8)
decisions.title: Access to Accounts — Replay Resistant
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: There is no authentication exchange that could be replayed; see IA-2. Replay protection for the traffic itself comes from TLS when the deployment mounts it (SC-8, SC-23).
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: IA-2(12)
decisions.title: Acceptance of PIV Credentials
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: The image accepts no credentials at all, PIV included: it has no authentication path for a client to present one to; see IA-2.
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: IA-4
decisions.title: Identifier Management
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: The image manages no identifiers: it issues none, and the identity it runs as is assigned by the platform (IMG-11, IMG-12); see IA-2.
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: IA-4(4)
decisions.title: Identify User Status
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: There is no identifier to mark as belonging to a contractor or a foreign national, because the image manages none; see IA-4.
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: IA-5
decisions.title: Authenticator Management
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: The image manages no authenticators. It holds no password, key, or token of its own; the only secret it may be given is a TLS private key, which arrives as a read-only mounted file and is never written, logged, or placed in arguments or environment (IMG-16, ADR-0003).
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: IA-5(1)
decisions.title: Password-based Authentication
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: No password authenticates anything in the image: it stores none, prompts for none, and has no account a password could belong to; see IA-5.
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: IA-5(2)
decisions.title: Public Key-based Authentication
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: The image performs no public-key authentication of users. It does verify publisher signatures on its own inputs at build time, against a key pinned by full fingerprint (IMG-02), which is a different control (SI-7, CM-14).
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: IA-5(6)
decisions.title: Protection of Authenticators
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: The image protects the one authenticator it may be given, a TLS private key, as ADR-0003 requires: read-only, readable only by the container's user or a group it belongs to, never in arguments, environment, or logs. The smoke suite proves the key does not appear in any of them (IMG-16).
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: IA-6
decisions.title: Authentication Feedback
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: The image gives no authentication feedback because it authenticates nobody; see IA-2. It also discloses no version in its responses, since server_tokens is off (SI-11).
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: IA-7
decisions.title: Cryptographic Module Authentication
decisions.rationale: The image authenticates to no cryptographic module; it makes no FIPS claim.
decisions.statement: The image authenticates to no cryptographic module. It uses OpenSSL as Red Hat ships it, for TLS when a deployment mounts key material, and makes no FIPS claim; how this standard treats images that protect CUI is open (SC-13).
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: IA-8
decisions.title: Identification and Authentication (Non-organizational Users)
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: The image identifies and authenticates no non-organizational user, serving every request anonymously; see IA-2.
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: IA-8(1)
decisions.title: Acceptance of PIV Credentials from Other Agencies
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: The image accepts no PIV credentials from other agencies, accepting no credentials at all; see IA-8.
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: IA-8(2)
decisions.title: Acceptance of External Authenticators
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: The image accepts no external authenticators, such as a federated or third-party credential, because it authenticates nobody; see IA-8.
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: IA-8(4)
decisions.title: Use of Defined Profiles
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: The image conforms to no identity profile because it performs no identification; see IA-8.
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: IA-11
decisions.title: Re-authentication
decisions.rationale: The image has no user accounts, logon, sessions, or authenticators: it serves static content to anonymous clients.
decisions.statement: There is no session to re-authenticate; each request is anonymous and independent; see IA-2.
decisions.warning: If the image authenticates any client, by password, token, certificate, API key, or S3 access key, it has accounts or authenticators, and not-applicable does not fit; decide what the image does with them.

decisions.label: SC-8
decisions.title: Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity
decisions.rationale: TLS protects transmission when the deployment mounts it; the image serves plain HTTP on 8080 otherwise.
decisions.statement: The image serves plain HTTP on 8080 as shipped, and TLS 1.2 or 1.3 on 8443 when the deployment mounts a server block, certificate, and key (IMG-16), which the smoke suite proves works. Whether transmission is protected in a given deployment therefore depends on that deployment, and on the platform's requirement that service traffic be encrypted (PLT-10, PLT-18).

decisions.label: SC-8(1)
decisions.title: Cryptographic Protection
decisions.rationale: As SC-8: TLS 1.2 and 1.3, when the deployment mounts it.
decisions.statement: The cryptography, when a deployment enables TLS, is OpenSSL as Red Hat ships it, restricted to TLS 1.2 and 1.3 by the server block the deployment mounts; the image ships no cipher policy of its own and makes no FIPS claim (SC-13, IA-7).

decisions.label: SC-10
decisions.title: Network Disconnect
decisions.rationale: Idle connections close after nginx's keepalive timeout; the deployment may set its own.
decisions.statement: The shipped configuration sets no keepalive_timeout, so nginx's default applies and idle connections close without intervention; a deployment that needs a specific period sets it in a mounted server block (IMG-16). Disconnecting a session on organizational policy is the deployment's and the platform's.

decisions.label: SC-13
decisions.title: Cryptographic Protection
decisions.rationale: nginx uses OpenSSL as shipped by Red Hat. The standard makes no FIPS claim, and its position on images that protect CUI is open.
decisions.statement: TLS, when a deployment enables it, uses OpenSSL as Red Hat ships it in UBI 9, pinned in the lock by digest and signature (IMG-02). The image makes no FIPS 140-3 claim: this standard has not yet decided what it requires of images that protect CUI, which is why this control stays open rather than being answered here.

decisions.label: SC-18
decisions.title: Mobile Code
decisions.rationale: Any script in the served content is the deployment's content, not the image's.
decisions.statement: The image ships one static HTML page and executes no mobile code: it has no scripting module, no CGI, and no application runtime, and the dynamic modules it carries are declared and verified (IMG-07). Any script in content a deployment mounts is that deployment's, to authorize under its own policy.

decisions.label: SC-23
decisions.title: Session Authenticity
decisions.rationale: Session authenticity is TLS, when the deployment mounts it.
decisions.statement: Session authenticity, for a protocol that keeps no session, is the authenticity of the connection: TLS when the deployment mounts it (SC-8), and the platform's mutual authentication between services (PLT-18). The image adds no session identifier, cookie, or token of its own.

decisions.label: SI-4(10)
decisions.title: Visibility of Encrypted Communications
decisions.rationale: The image does not monitor traffic; that is the platform's (PLT-16).
decisions.statement: The image neither inspects nor monitors traffic, encrypted or otherwise; it answers requests. Making encrypted communications visible to monitoring is the platform's (PLT-16, PLT-10), which is where this standard places it.

decisions.label: SI-8
decisions.title: Spam Protection
decisions.rationale: The image handles no mail.
decisions.statement: The image handles no electronic mail: it has no mail transfer agent, no mail client, and no mailbox, and its only listeners are the declared HTTP ports (IMG-30).

decisions.label: SI-8(2)
decisions.title: Automatic Updates
decisions.rationale: The image handles no mail.
decisions.statement: There are no spam-protection mechanisms to update, since the image handles no mail; see SI-8. The image's own inputs are kept current by a reviewed refresh (IMG-04, IMG-29).

decisions.label: SI-10
decisions.title: Information Input Validation
decisions.rationale: nginx rejects malformed requests, but no criterion yet evidences it.
decisions.statement: nginx parses and rejects malformed requests, answering 400 rather than passing them on, and the image passes no input to an interpreter or application runtime because it hosts none. What is missing is a criterion and a check that prove the rejection, rather than relying on nginx's behaviour, which is why this control stays open.

decisions.label: SI-11
decisions.title: Error Handling
decisions.rationale: server_tokens is off, so errors do not disclose the version, but no criterion yet evidences error handling.
decisions.statement: The shipped configuration sets server_tokens off, so error responses carry neither the version nor build details, and errors go to standard error rather than to a client. What is missing is a criterion that requires error output be free of internal detail, and a check for it, which is why this control stays open.
